note: Miss and overconfidence. Boston led the series 3-2, but Philadelphia had just won Game 5 by 16 and Joel Embiid had returned with 33 points. An 82% forecast discounted both the demonstrated swing in team strength and the substantial uncertainty of two remaining games; live playoff series with a newly returned star need less concentration.

Top-outcome hit. Antonelli had taken the prior two poles while Mercedes produced three consecutive front-row lockouts, so the performance trend correctly outweighed the uncertainty introduced by rival upgrades.

Covered outcome, though not top-ranked. Leclerc's previous third-place qualifying result and Ferrari's expected Miami strength warranted his 19% share. The broad distribution appropriately reflected the volatility of an exact grid-position market.

Candidate-set miss. The forecast omitted one of the four Grand Slam organizers even though the dispute concerned all majors. When an institutional question can resolve to any member of a small, known set, cover the complete set before assigning weight to a semantically related but structurally different body such as the ITF.

Candidate-set miss. Final-post analysis concentrated on five prominent contenders but omitted Golden Tempo in a 20-horse field. Leaving probability unassigned does not protect an unnamed winner under the scoring rule; for large-field races, preserve at least one explicit slot for a credible longer-priced runner selected from the complete field.
